heroHeadline: Senate Parliamentarian Strikes Major ICE/CBP Reconciliation Provisions Under Byrd Rule; Federal Judge Halts Texas SB 4 State Deportation Law; ICE Warehouse Detention Expansion Proceeds in San Antonio and Socorro Despite Federal Probe
heroSubtitle: On May 14–15, 2026, Senate Parliamentarian Elizabeth MacDonough struck major HSGAC sections of the $71.7 billion reconciliation package as Byrd Rule violations — including main Border Patrol funding, DHS appropriations, and border security/technology/screening provisions — forcing Republicans to rewrite significant portions before the scheduled May 18 Senate floor vote with Trump's June 1 signing deadline looming. Separately, U.S. District Judge David Alan Ezra (W.D. Tex.) halted the core provisions of Texas SB 4 on May 14, the day before the state law was set to take effect — blocking state magistrate deportation orders, reentry criminalization, and enforcement penalty provisions while allowing only the illegal entry provision to proceed; the ACLU, ACLU of Texas, and Texas Civil Rights Project filed the class-action challenge May 4. A federal court on May 15 ordered ICE to immediately release José Francisco Orellana-Rivera, a Honduran man brought to the U.S. at age four with DACA protection and two U.S.-citizen children, finding he was detained without the required bond hearing — the latest in more than 10,000 judicial rulings against ICE detention practices since January 2025. The Washington Post reported May 14 that ICE is proceeding with warehouse detention contracts in San Antonio and Socorro despite a federal probe and multiple lawsuits; Human Rights First documented ICE Air reaching a record 245 deportation flights in April 2026, including first-ever forced transfers to Uganda, Paraguay, and the DRC and a single 51-hour multi-country flight with detainees restrained throughout. FY2026 deaths in ICE custody stand at 30+ with 152 new detention facilities opened across 39 states since January 2025.
footerNote: Data sourced from DHS, ICE official records, ACLU, HRW, DHS OIG, TRAC Reports, Detention Watch Network, USCIS, ILRC, NIPNLG, Human Rights First, court records, Senate Budget Committee, and Congressional records
